title: Lift closed-fibre kernel parameters while retaining the given base parameters
statement: Let A,B be Noetherian local rings and R,S regular local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let f:A -> B, q:R -> A, b:S -> B and i:R -> S be local homomorphisms, with q and b surjective and b i = f q. Let t be a regular parameter system of R, and (i(t),z) one of S [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Put I=m_A B. Give B/I its quotient algebra structure over A/m_A [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Assume it is formally smooth for the image of m_B [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Then there are lists x,y in S such that (x,i(t),y) is a regular parameter system, (x) is contained in ker b, and ker(S -> B -> B/I)=(x)+m_R S. No flatness or coefficient-ring assumption is made.

source.place: Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) implies (3), compatible presentation through the displayed isomorphism S tensor_R A -> B; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NQ.

proof.text: The proper ideal I=m_A B gives E=B/I its local Noetherian quotient structure. Rewrite the image of m_B as m_E and apply adic formal smoothness over the residue field to obtain regular locality of E.

Put M=m_R S=(i(t)). The initial-parameter quotient theorem makes S/M regular local of dimension length(z). Surjectivity of q identifies its image of m_R with m_A; compatibility and surjectivity of b show b(M)=I. Thus b induces a surjection w:S/M -> E. Identify its kernel quotient with E and obtain a full parameter list bs whose first c entries generate ker w.

Lift each of the first c entries of bs to s in S. Since b(s) is in I=b(M), choose s' in M with b(s')=b(s), and replace s by s-s'. These corrected lifts x lie in ker b and have the same classes modulo M. Lift the remaining entries to y. List induction realizes the two finite lists in Lean.

The ideal generated by (i(t),x,y) contains M and maps onto the maximal ideal of S/M; its preimage is m_S. The full lifted list has the same length as (i(t),z), so it is a parameter system. Permute it to (x,i(t),y). Pulling ker w back along S -> S/M gives the claimed kernel identity.

theorem exists_closedFiber_kernel_parameters
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) (R : Type w) (S : Type x)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsRegularLocalRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing S]
    (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f]
    (q : R →+* A) [IsLocalHom q] (b : S →+* B) [IsLocalHom b]
    (i : R →+* S) [IsLocalHom i]
    (hq : Function.Surjective q) (hb : Function.Surjective b)
    (hcomm : b.comp i = f.comp q)
    (t : List R) (z : List S)
    (ht : IsRegularSystemOfParameters t)
    (hz : IsRegularSystemOfParameters (t.map i ++ z)) :
    letI : Algebra A B := f.toAlgebra
    let I : Ideal B := (maximalIdeal A).map f
    letI : Algebra (A ⧸ maximalIdeal A) (B ⧸ I) :=
      Ideal.Quotient.algebraQuotientOfLEComap (Ideal.le_comap_map :
        maximalIdeal A ≤ I.comap (algebraMap A B))
    Algebra.FormallySmoothAdic (A ⧸ maximalIdeal A) (B ⧸ I)
      ((maximalIdeal B).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) →
    ∃ x y : List S,
      IsRegularSystemOfParameters (x ++ (t.map i ++ y)) ∧
      Ideal.ofList x ≤ RingHom.ker b ∧
      RingHom.ker ((Ideal.Quotient.mk I).comp b) =
        Ideal.ofList x ⊔ (maximalIdeal R).map i
